Infra & Chips.content: ![](https://sb.scorecardresearch.com/p?c1=2&c2=16433046&cv=3.9.1&cj=1) ## ## Latest in ## More # Nvidia vs. AMD: Elon Musk Picked a Side on the SpaceX Earnings Call ## Key Points Nvidia and AMD are the two leading GPU designers for artificial intelligence (AI) workloads. Elon Musk has spoken highly about Nvidia's GPUs in the past, and did so again during SpaceX's earnings call. Nvidia GPUs are now used in operations at both Tesla and SpaceX, the latter of which has turned its chip procurement into a lucrative AI infrastructure business. The GPU market is dominated by a duopoly featuring **Nvidia**(NASDAQ: NVDA) and **Advanced Micro Devices**(NASDAQ: AMD). Nvidia is shipping Blackwell at enormous scale and ramping up [Vera Rubin](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/04/prediction-vera-rubin-is-about-to-become-a-20-bil/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=f39243d4-7089-4efe-a269-f5e6f7ca9b0a) as the next rack-scale platform. Meanwhile, AMD is selling MI300 systems and lining up its next-generation MI400 accelerators to keep its seat at the table. **Amazon**, **Alphabet**, **Microsoft**, **Oracle**, **Meta Platforms**, Anthropic, and OpenAI are not picking one vendor to supply chips for the artificial intelligence (AI) build-outs. Instead, they are stuffing solutions from both Nvidia and AMD into the same stacks because supply is tight, different workloads require specific architectures, and nobody can afford to sit around and wait. ***Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again.**In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. [**Continue »**](https://api.fool.com/infotron/infotrack/click?apikey=35527423-a535-4519-a07f-20014582e03e&impression=f5f73760-fa95-4bae-bbb8-ef7f1c6473ed&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fool.com%2Fmms%2Fmark%2Fa-sa-dd-total-conviction%3Faid%3D11123%26source%3Disaediica0000078%26ftm_cam%3Dsa-dd-4%26ftm_veh%3Dtop_incontent_pitch_feed_partner%26ftm_pit%3D19478&utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=f39243d4-7089-4efe-a269-f5e6f7ca9b0a)* This is the backdrop of the AI infrastructure landscape. However, during **Space Exploration Technologies**' first earnings call as a public company, [Elon Musk](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/famous-investors/elon-musk-investments/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=f39243d4-7089-4efe-a269-f5e6f7ca9b0a) stepped into the chip arena and made his preference abundantly obvious. ![AMD and Nvidia logos.](https://barchart-news-media-prod.aws.barchart.com/FC/46686d88dd5f432e88effa5155df99ae/%3Furl%3Dhttps%253a%252f%252fg.foolcdn.com%252feditorial%252fimages%252f887069%252famd-and-nvda-logos.png%26amp%3Bw%3D700) Image source: The Motley Fool. ## Musk is not hedging his bets During SpaceX's second-quarter earnings call, Musk did not leave much room for interpretation. He stated: [G]oing forward, we've decided to build exclusively on Nvidia because we think the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture. We think it's the best AI computer, and we greatly value our close cooperation and partnership on many levels with Nvidia. So we're exclusive to Nvidia. This really isn't a shock to anyone who has watched **Tesla** over the years. Tesla trains some of its autonomy stack on Nvidia's hardware even while the company works on its own inference chips for [robotaxi](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/03/bull-vs-bear-heres-my-take-tesla-robotaxi-rollout/?utm_source=globeandmail&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=f39243d4-7089-4efe-a269-f5e6f7ca9b0a) and Optimus. the plan](//www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-04/deepseek-plans-big-huawei-ai-chip-order-to-power-new-data-center). Scheduled to partially come online by late 2027 or early 2028, this facility will form one of the largest known clusters of Chinese-made AI chips. Neither company has commented. To understand this move, it helps to view AI computing through a simple analogy. Training is like a student studying a vast library of books for years, requiring immense, specialised brainpower. Inference is that same student taking an exam, answering questions efficiently based on what they learned. Because of ongoing trade restrictions, DeepSeek is splitting these tasks. The heavy lifting of training new models remains on whatever Nvidia hardware the company can secure. Inference, running the models for everyday users, will move to the new Huawei 950DT chips. Huawei designed the Ascend 950DT for training, and DeepSeek is not using it for that. ## The facility and the hardware Located 350km north-west of Beijing, Ulanqab has cheap wind and solar energy, coupled with an average temperature of 4.3°C for natural cooling. At full load, the one-gigawatt site will consume enough power for 750,000 homes. Historically reliant on rented computing, DeepSeek [raised over $7 billion in June 2026](/2026/07/07/deepseek-own-ai-inference-chip-nvidia-huawei/) to fund this physical infrastructure. The research was published by invitation in Nature Reviews Electrical Engineering (NREE), a journal published by Nature. The study centers on integrating CPUs, accelerators, and memory into a single datacenter-scale domain based on the [CXL](https://en.wowtale.net/tag/CXL) (Compute Express Link) standard. Compared to NVIDIA’s representative rack-scale system GB200 NVL72, the unified accelerator connection scale increases approximately thirteen-fold, while cross-rack access latency drops to nanosecond-level speeds—up to one-tenth the previous time. As AI models grow to trillion-parameter scales, hundreds to thousands of accelerators participate in a single training step and exchange terabyte-level data.
